answer.evidence: The entire streetlamp is drawn in pure front elevation: the upper grey section (rows 0-4) is the vertical front face/cap of the lantern head rather than a receding horizontal top surface, with perfectly horizontal straight boundaries across the cap, glowing band, and lower housing. No horizontal surface foreshortened in 3/4 perspective is visible on the lamp head or post.

The wide top surface of the lamp head is explicitly rendered from rows 0 to 4 (5 rows tall) with an inset paneled top face before transitioning to the south-facing emissive band (rows 6-7) and tapered lower section. The ground light pool at rows 28-31 also confirms the 3/4 downward angle.

The top surface of the lamp head is clearly rendered across rows 1-4 (4 pixel rows tall) above the downward-facing light band and housing. The base also features an elliptical light puddle on the ground plane, consistent with 3/4 top-down perspective.

The entire street lamp is drawn in pure front elevation: the lamp head cap (rows 1-4) has straight vertical side outlines and a straight horizontal base (row 5) with no elliptical foreshortening to indicate a top surface viewed from a 45-degree angle. The light band, stem, and base plinth (rows 26-29) are all rendered with flat, straight horizontal edges.
